title: Reading Level
summary: Flags copy that reads above its audience's grade level and points at the sentences and wordy phrases that cause it.
description: Live Flesch-Kincaid grade against a target. Tints the hardest sentences in place (only when long and dense), with the reason and a jump to each, and offers one-tap plain-word swaps ("utilize" → "use").
catches: Grade above the target you set (default 8)
Sentences that are both long and dense, tinted in place
Wordy words and phrases with a plainer swap
Non-English text, where it shows a notice instead of a grade
limits: Syllables are estimated from vowel groups (roughly ±10%), so grades are approximate
Flesch-Kincaid is an English-only formula and ignores meaning, layout and audience
The swap list is a starter set; it will miss domain jargon
a11y: Visible <label> tied to the textarea, with the grade wired via aria-describedby
On/above-target status announced through a polite sr-only live region
Each swap button has an aria-label naming the word and its replacement
After a swap, focus moves to the next swap button (or back to the field)
The tinted backdrop is aria-hidden; sentence difficulty also shown as text
stops: Copy harder to read than its audience needs
